gloss: to wipe out (a disgrace); to avenge; to clear (one's name)

definitions.gloss: to wipe out (a disgrace); to avenge; to clear (one's name)
definitions.explanation: To remove or make up for a disgrace, dishonor, or humiliating defeat, typically by achieving a later success or victory. A formal, somewhat literary word, most often used with objects such as {恥|はじ} (shame) or {汚名|おめい} (a bad name).

examples.japanese: ⟦{前回|ぜんかい}→前回：11817_zenkai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{負|ま}け→負け：02569_make⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{雪|そそ}いだ。

⟦{汚名|おめい}→汚名：13265_omei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{雪|そそ}ぐ⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦もう{一度|いちど}→もう一度：02976_mouichido⟧⟦{挑戦|ちょうせん}する→挑戦する：21602_chousensuru⟧こと⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{決|き}めた→決める：00858_kimeru⟧。
examples.english: In order to clear his tarnished name, he decided to take on the challenge once more.

notes:
A formal, literary verb meaning to erase a disgrace by a subsequent achievement.

TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive; the thing wiped out (a disgrace, defeat, or bad reputation) takes ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{恥|はじ}→恥：12636_haji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{雪|そそ}ぐ: to wipe out one's shame
- ⟦{汚名|おめい}→汚名：13265_omei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{雪|そそ}ぐ: to clear one's tarnished name
- ⟦{雪辱|せつじょく}→雪辱：19575_setsujoku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{果|は}たす→果たす：10060_hatasu⟧: to achieve one's revenge (the related noun ⟦{雪辱|せつじょく}→雪辱：19575_setsujoku⟧ is far more common in everyday speech)

USAGE:
The kanji {雪|そそ}ぐ is also read すすぐ, which more usually means "to rinse" (also written ⟦{濯|すす}ぐ→濯ぐ：04263_susugu⟧). In the "wipe out a disgrace" sense, the reading そそぐ is standard. Note this word is distinct from ⟦{注|そそ}ぐ→注ぐ：02124_sosogu⟧ (to pour), a homophone.
